GitHub indicates that CVE requests for repository security advisories must be initiated by repository maintainers or owners. # Conditional stored admin XSS via failed-job details High freescout-help-desk published GHSA-2g42-f97q-973x Aug 14, 2026 ## Package freescout-help-desk/freescout (Composer) ## Affected versions <1.8.230 ## Patched versions 1.8.230 ## Description ## Summary FreeScout 1.8.229 contains a conditional stored cross-site scripting issue in the administrator failed-job details view. A pre-authenticated attacker can place an HTML payload in a failed login email value. If Logs Monitoring is enabled for the `users` activity log and the resulting alert email job fails, the payload is stored in the serialized `SendAlert` job payload in `failed_jobs`. An administrator who opens the affected `/system/ajax-html/job_details/{id}` response as a top-level page receives a raw HTML fragment without the normal layout CSP, allowing inline event-handler JavaScript such as `` to execute in the administrator's authenticated browser context. The normal System Status modal path is not claimed to execute the payload: it is blocked by the parent page CSP in the tested version. This report is limited to the top-level failed-job-details path and the configuration/error conditions described below. ## Affected Versions * Tested version: FreeScout 1.8.229. * Potentially affected versions: not exhaustively bisected. Versions with the same failed login logging, Logs Monitoring alert, `SendAlert` queue, failed-job detail rendering, and `stripDangerousTags` behavior are expected to be affected. ## Environment * Local authorized Docker deployment on a reporter-controlled host. * Web access was tunneled to `http://localhost:18080`. * Database access was tunneled to `127.0.0.1:18306`. * The validation environment used the FreeScout 1.8.229 source tree. ## Prerequisites * The initial payload injection is pre-authenticated: the attacker only needs network access to the login form and a valid CSRF token from that form. * Logs Monitoring must be enabled and configured to monitor the `users` activity log. In code, this corresponds to `config('app.alert_logs')`, a configured `alert_logs_period`, and `alert_logs_names` containing `users`. * The scheduled Logs Monitoring command or an equivalent manual execution must run after the failed-login activity is stored. * System alert email delivery must fail so that the `SendAlert` queued job is moved to `failed_jobs`. A healthy alert-mail configuration sends the alert successfully and does not create the failed-job sink used by this proof. * An authenticated administrator must open the affected failed-job details URL as a top-level page or new tab, for example `/system/ajax-html/job_details/{id}`. The normal modal opened from System > Status was observed to be CSP-blocked and is not the claimed trigger. * Queue workers must process the `emails` queue and eventually mark the failing `SendAlert` job as failed. The local proof used `queue:work database --queue=emails --once --tries=1` to make the condition deterministic. ## Vulnerability Details The issue is a multi-step stored XSS path from a pre-authenticated input source into an administrator-only failed-job diagnostic sink. 1. Pre-authenticated source: `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/LoginController.php:50-77` calls `validateLogin()` and then returns a failed login response on unsuccessful authentication. The Laravel trait validation in `vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Foundation/Auth/AuthenticatesUsers.php:60-65` requires the username field only to be a string, not an RFC-valid email address. The failed login event is wired in `app/Providers/EventServiceProvider.php:34-35`, and `app/Listeners/LogFailedLogin.php:30-34` records `request()->email` verbatim into `activity_logs.properties` under `ActivityLog::NAME_USER`, whose value is `users` in `app/ActivityLog.php:9`. 2. Logs Monitoring propagation: `app/Console/Kernel.php:81-88` schedules Logs Monitoring when alert logging is enabled and a period is configured. `app/Console/Commands/LogsMonitor.php:89-92` selects records whose `log_name` is in the configured monitored set. `app/Console/Commands/LogsMonitor.php:111-121` concatenates each selected log's `$log->properties` into an HTML alert body and passes that body to `MailHelper::sendAlertMail()`. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Deploy FreeScout 1.8.229 locally. 2. Enable Logs Monitoring for the `users` activity log and configure a monitoring period. 3. Configure system alert mail so that the `SendAlert` job fails during delivery, for example by pointing the local test instance at an unreachable SMTP service. 4. From an unauthenticated browser session, load `/login` to obtain the form CSRF token. 5. Submit a failed login with the attacker-controlled HTML payload in the email field. 6. Run the Logs Monitoring command so that the failed-login activity record is included in the alert body. 7. Process the `emails` queue until the alert job fails and appears in `failed_jobs`. 8. As an administrator, open the affected `/system/ajax-html/job_details/{id}` URL as a top-level page or new tab. 9. Observe that the surviving HTML payload executes in the administrator browser context. In the local impact proof, the top-level XSS created a temporary administrator account and then verified that the new administrator could access `/users/wizard`. ## Proof of Concept `The following local PoC scripts were run against the authorized local Docker instance: ./local_poc/F-system-tools-1_failed-job-payload-top-level-xss_local.sh ./local_poc/F-system-tools-1_admin-impact-xss_local.sh Representative validated output from the top-level payload proof: pre-auth failed login HTTP=302 activity_log marker row= queued SendAlert job= failed_jobs marker row= modal_like_spv=script-src-attr|inline top_level_exec=True PASS: pre-auth failed-login payload reached failed_jobs.payload and executed on direct top-level job_details navigation Representative validated output from the impact proof: [*] pre-auth failed login HTTP=302 marker=SRCMK-fsauditlocal-98aa4c8612a3 [*] activity_log marker row=249 [*] queued SendAlert job=18 [*] failed_jobs marker row=23 window_name=impact:200:200:true [*] created_admin_user_id=9 email=xss-admin-fsauditlocal-98aa4c8612a3@local.test new_admin_users_wizard_status=200 new_admin_access_denied=False new_admin_url=http://localhost:18080/users/wizard PASS: top-level job_details XSS created a temporary role=2 administrator user and that user reached /users/wizard Cleanup was verified after the run: xss_admin_users 0 marker_activity 0 marker_jobs 0 marker_failed_jobs 0 ` * The local impact proof used that context to fetch `/users/wizard`, extract the CSRF token, submit a user-creation request with `role=2`, and verify that the new temporary administrator could access `/users/wizard`. This can lead to administrator account creation or other administrator-context actions if the required configuration, alert-mail failure, and top-level administrator interaction occur. Important limitations: * The normal System Status modal path was observed to be blocked by CSP and is not claimed as an executing trigger. * This is not a default, unconditional exploit path. Logs Monitoring for `users`, alert-mail failure, queue failure handling, and top-level administrator viewing are required. * The report does not claim cookie theft; HTTP-only cookie settings may prevent direct cookie reads. The demonstrated impact uses same-origin administrator requests instead. ## CVSS Assessment * Proposed CVSS version: 3.1 * Proposed vector: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` * Proposed score: 7.5 High * Rationale: the attacker-controlled source is network-accessible and pre-authenticated, but exploitation requires several environmental conditions that the attacker may not control, including Logs Monitoring configuration, alert-mail delivery failure, failed queue storage, and an administrator opening the raw job-details URL as a top-level page. Successful exploitation runs JavaScript in an administrator session and can perform high-impact same-origin actions, including administrator account creation in the validated local proof. ## CWE * CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Stored XSS in site name rendered without escaping · Advisory · craftcms/cms · GitHub (https://github.com/craftcms/cms/security/advisories/GHSA-5fjj-496j-2qqf) 【turn766819search1】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 2 months ago; Crawled: last month; A stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the site name field. ... * `allowAdminChanges` must be enabled. # Stored XSS in site name rendered without escaping Low angrybrad published GHSA-5fjj-496j-2qqf Aug 18, 2026 ## Software craftcms/cms ## Affected versions >= 5.0.0-RC1, < 5.10.11 ## Patched versions 5.10.11 ## Description A stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the site name field. The application fails to sanitize input, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript when another user views a page with the malicious table field. ## Required Permissions * Administrator account * `allowAdminChanges` must be enabled. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Log in to the CP as admin. 2. Settings > Sites > create or rename a site. Set the Name to any XSS payload. 3. Navigate to Settings > Email & Notice the XSS execution. ## Impact Stored XSS in the control panel. Scope: More severe when a scope change occurs, e.g. one vulnerable component impacts resources in components beyond its security scope. # Stored XSS in Admin Stats Interface (/stats?format=html) High phlax published GHSA-pv9h-4fxf-7vrg Aug 26, 2026 ## Package Envoy (Envoy Proxy) ## Affected versions <1.40.0 ## Patched versions 1.39.1, 1.38.4, 1.37.6, 1.36.10 ## Description ## Vulnerability Details Vulnerability Type: Cross-Site Scripting (Stored XSS) Component: `source/server/admin/` (Envoy Admin Interface) Severity: MEDIUM (Exploitable Stored XSS on Trusted Admin Surface) Affected Code: `stats_html_render.cc:58-62` and `stats_html_render.h:34` ### Description Envoy's administration interface exposes `/stats?format=html`, which formats and displays the current counters, gauges, and histograms. When generating the HTML output, `StatsHtmlRender` correctly sanitizes stat values (when they are strings), but fails to sanitize the stat names themselves. In `stats_html_render.cc:58`, the string-value overload directly emits `name` raw: void StatsHtmlRender::generate(Buffer::Instance& response, const std::string& name, When enabled, `resolveServiceAndMethod` strictly splits the `:path` header and injects the attacker-controlled segments into `Stats::DynamicSavedName`. 3. An administrator or automated tool must view the `/stats?format=html` endpoint via a web browser. ### Impact Since the XSS executes in the context of the Envoy administration dashboard, the JavaScript payload runs Same-Origin to the admin port. From here, the attacker's script can make unauthorized synchronous or asynchronous `POST` requests to highly privileged admin endpoints. For instance: * `POST /quitquitquit`: Forcefully terminates the Envoy process resulting in a Denial of Service. * `POST /runtime_modify?key=value`: Manipulates memory limits, circuit breakers, or critical feature flags dynamically. ## Mitigation The patch requires HTML sanitization wrapped around the emitted `name` within `StatsHtmlRender`. Code Fix: Ensure `Html::Utility::sanitize` is applied to keys: // In stats_html_render.cc void StatsHtmlRender::generate(Buffer::Instance& response, const std::string& name, const std::string& value) { response.addFragments({Html::Utility::sanitize(name), ": \"", Html::Utility::sanitize(value), "\"\n"}); } // In stats_html_render.h void generate(Buffer::Instance& response, const std::string& name, uint64_t value) override { response.addFragments({Html::Utility::sanitize(name), ": ", absl::StrCat(value), "\n"}); } -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Stored XSS in the group member table: escapeHtml output concatenated into tel:, mailto: and data-name attributes allows a non-admin to run script in an administrator's session · Advisory · ChurchCRM/CRM · GitHub (https://github.com/ChurchCRM/CRM/security/advisories/GHSA-m649-24q9-q6r4) 【turn766819search8】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 2 months ago; Crawled: 2 months ago; # Stored XSS in the group member table: escapeHtml output concatenated into tel:, mailto: and data-name attributes allows a non-admin to run script in an administrator's session ... * `PR:L`: storing the payload needs only `usr_EditRecords`; the account used had `usr_Admin=0`. ... Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-42Mpi7KQ... ... Distinction from prior advisories # Stored XSS in the group member table: escapeHtml output concatenated into tel:, mailto: and data-name attributes allows a non-admin to run script in an administrator's session High DawoudIO published GHSA-m649-24q9-q6r4 Aug 10, 2026 ## Package churchcrm/crm (Composer) ## Affected versions 7.5.1 ## Patched versions 7.6.0 ## Description ## 1. Summary Three DataTables render callbacks in `src/skin/js/GroupView.js` build HTML attributes by concatenating `$("
").text(v).html()` output: the `tel:` href at `:771-772`, the `mailto:` href at `:782-783`, and `data-name` at `:794`/`:824-825`. That idiom encodes `<`, `>` and `&` but not `"`, so a stored value containing a double quote closes the attribute and the remainder is parsed as further attributes. A person's cell phone, email or full name — writable by any account with `EditRecords`, no admin rights — therefore becomes a live event handler in the browser of every user who opens the group, including an administrator. The encoder in use is the inline equivalent of `window.CRM.escapeHtml`. That helper's own doc comment at `src/skin/js/CRMJSOM.js:24-31` records that it does not encode quotes, which is why `escapeAttribute` was added beside it at `:32`. Neither named helper is called at these three sinks; the idiom is spelled out inline instead. `alert(1)` fires in a real Chrome session authenticated as `Admin` after `tony.wade` (`usr_Admin=0`) saves the payload. ## 2. Severity / CVSS `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N` — 8.7 (High) * `PR:L`: storing the payload needs only `usr_EditRecords`; the account used had `usr_Admin=0`. * `UI:R`: the proven variant fires on hover. The `data-name` sink in the same row takes `autofocus onfocus=`, which needs no interaction and would score `UI:N`, 9.0. The lower score is claimed. * `S:C`: the script runs with the viewing administrator's session authority, a different scope from the attacker's account. * CSP is emitted report-only by default (`bEnforceCSP` false), so inline handlers execute. Under an enforcing header this degrades to defacement rather than script execution. Preconditions: any account with `EditRecords` or `AddRecords`; attacker and victim share a group; the victim opens `/groups/view/{id}`. Default configuration. CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation. CWE-116 Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output. ## 5. Impact * Non-admin to admin script execution. `alert(1)` captured from a Chrome dialog handler in a session authenticated as `Admin`; the parsed DOM attribute `onmouseover` read back as `alert(1)`. * Attribute injection, not tag injection. The payload `5" onmouseover=alert(1) x="` contains no `<`, so `strip_tags` is a no-op on it. * Same-origin with the victim's cookie. The injected handler can call any endpoint the viewing administrator can, including `/admin/api/user/{id}/password/reset` and user creation. * Three fields, one row. Cell phone, email and full name all reach attribute context from the same API response. ## 6. Proof of Concept ### A. Store the payload as a non-admin `tony.wade` has `usr_Admin=0`, `usr_EditRecords=1`. The PersonEditor form for person 2 is replayed with one field changed. `CellPhone=5" onmouseover=alert(1) x=" PersonSubmit=Save HTTP/1.1 200 ` ### B. The API hands the raw quote to the client `$ curl -s -H 'x-api-key: ' http://localhost:8099/api/groups/1/members ... "CellPhone":"5\" onmouseover=alert(1) x=\"" ... ` ### C. Render in an administrator's browser Real Chrome, logged in through `POST /session/begin` as `Admin`, navigated to `/groups/view/1`, hovered the phone link. `$ python3 verify.py store payload as non-admin -> 200 [payload] parsed onmouseover attribute: 'alert(1)' [payload] dialogs captured: ['1'] ` The browser exposes `onmouseover` as a real attribute, so this is handler execution rather than unescaped source text. ### D. Control, benign value, same account and same page `store benign as non-admin -> 200 [control] parsed onmouseover attribute: None [control] dialogs captured: [] ` Stored value `(003)-025-4087` renders as ``. The quote, not the presence of user data, is what breaks the attribute. ### E. No CSP obstacle `$ curl -sI http://localhost:8099/session/begin | grep -i content-security Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-42Mpi7KQ... ` A through E reproduced at commit `24869b1e`. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- listmonk Vulnerable to Stored XSS Leading to Admin Account Takeover · CVE-2026-21483 · GitHub Advisory Database · GitHub (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jmr4-p576-v565) 【turn766819search9】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 10 months ago; Crawled: 2 months ago; ## listmonk Vulnerable to Stored XSS Leading to Admin Account Takeover ... github.com/knadh/listmonk (Go) ... ## Security Advisory: Stored XSS Leading to Admin Account Takeover ## listmonk Vulnerable to Stored XSS Leading to Admin Account Takeover Moderate severity GitHub Reviewed Published Jan 2, 2026 in knadh/listmonk • Updated Jan 2, 2026 Vulnerability details Dependabot alerts 0 ## Package github.com/knadh/listmonk (Go) ## Affected versions >= 1.1.1, < 6.0.0 < 1.1.1-0.20251231125615-74dc5a01cfbb ## Patched versions 6.0.0 1.1.1-0.20251231125615-74dc5a01cfbb ## Description ## Security Advisory: Stored XSS Leading to Admin Account Takeover Affected Versions: ≤ 5.1.0 Vulnerability Type: CWE-79: Stored Cross-Site Scripting * * * ## Summary A lower-privileged user with campaign management permissions can inject malicious JavaScript into campaigns or templates. When a higher-privileged user (Super Admin) views or previews this content, the XSS executes in their browser context, allowing the attacker to perform privileged actions such as creating backdoor admin accounts. The attack can be weaponized via the public archive feature, where victims simply need to visit a link - no preview click required. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- CI4MS: Profile & User Management Full Account Takeover for All-Roles & Privilege-Escalation via Stored DOM XSS · CVE-2026-34989 · GitHub Advisory Database · GitHub (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vr2g-rhm5-q4jr) 【turn766819search10】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 7 months ago; Crawled: 2 months ago; Critical severity GitHub Reviewed Published Apr 2, 2026 in ci4-cms-erp/ci4ms • Updated May 5, 2026 ...
